column4: God gives Thamud the she-camel as a visible sign, but they wrong her (ءَاتَيْنَا ثَمُودَ النَّاقَةَ مُبْصِرَةً فَظَلَمُوا بِهَا); this directly ties the section's camel to divine sending and the community's transgression.

God says He sent (بَعَثْنَا) a messenger to every community, calling them to worship Him and avoid false gods; this states the divine sending side of the section's contrast with the man who launches himself into rebellion.

After rain makes the earth's vegetation flourish, God's command comes by night or day and leaves it harvested (فَجَعَلْنَاهَا حَصِيدًا); this joins the section's crop and night-covering images in a sudden reversal.
A good word is compared to a firmly rooted tree whose branches reach the sky (كَشَجَرَةٍ طَيِّبَةٍ); this makes the section's two moral courses perceptible as different growth rooted within.

The bad word is a tree uprooted from the earth without stability (كَشَجَرَةٍ خَبِيثَةٍ اجْتُثَّتْ); this completes the previous ayah's fruitful tree with a clear counterpart to the section's buried, unproductive field.

Salih says God brought the people forth from the earth (أَنشَأَكُم مِّنَ الْأَرْضِ); this links the messenger's address to the section's earth as the ground of human formation and Thamud's settlement.
The record of the wicked (كِتَابَ الْفُجَّارِ) is placed in Sijjīn; this repeats the section's fujūr category and gives its morally buried course a recorded destination.

This verse says people's earnings have left rust over their hearts (رَانَ عَلَىٰ قُلُوبِهِم); it contrasts the section's torn protective veil with a covering produced by sin that instead obscures the inner self.

A wall with a gate separates believers from hypocrites at the final judgment (بَيْنَهُم بِسُورٍ لَّهُ بَابٌ); it develops the section's taqwa-as-boundary image into a last separation between two outcomes.

Turning back on one's heels (يَنقَلِبُ عَلَىٰ عَقِبَيْهِ) is a literal heel-branch in a passage about following or turning from the Messenger; it extends the section's heel/aftermath association into a different, directional sense.
Rain brings forth vegetation that later becomes dry fragments scattered by wind (هَشِيمًا تَذْرُوهُ الرِّيَاحُ); this is another concrete version of the section's watered field becoming barren.
The good tree bears its fruit at every season (تُؤْتِي أُكُلَهَا كُلَّ حِينٍ); this ayah contributes the productive outcome of the moral tree introduced just before it.

The verse asks people to consider how camels were created (إِلَى الْإِبِلِ كَيْفَ خُلِقَتْ); this places the divinely formed animal at the center of a created order that the section shows Thamud violating.
The next ayah asks how the sky was raised (السَّمَاءِ كَيْفَ رُفِعَتْ); it contributes the section's sky image to the same passage that begins with the camel.
The passage next asks how mountains were set firm (الْجِبَالِ كَيْفَ نُصِبَتْ); it places fixed terrain between the camel and the spread earth in the linked creation survey.
The earth is described as spread out (الْأَرْضِ كَيْفَ سُطِحَتْ); this completes that camel-to-sky-to-land sequence with the section's ground image.
